title: Tornado Emergency for Corwin: Statement on Warning 0071

fields.bulletin: *** EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE — NOT A REAL PRODUCT *** BULLETIN - EAS ACTIVATION REQUESTED
warningFor: Northern Brennan County in western Kentucky
fields.at: At 1051 PM CST, a confirmed large and destructive tornado was located over the southwest edge of Corwin, moving northeast at 60 mph. This is a TORNADO EMERGENCY for Corwin. THIS IS A PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. TAKE COVER NOW!
fields.source: Weather spotters confirmed tornado. Radar confirmed tornado debris.
fields.impact: You are in a life-threatening situation. Flying debris may be deadly to those caught without shelter. Mobile homes will be destroyed. Considerable damage to homes, businesses, and vehicles is likely and complete destruction is possible.
actions: To repeat, a large, extremely dangerous and potentially deadly tornado is on the ground in Corwin. To protect your life, TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows.
If you are outdoors, in a vehicle or in a mobile home, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Do not try to outrun this tornado in a vehicle.
This tornado is wrapped in heavy rain. Do not wait to see or hear it. TAKE COVER NOW! *** EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE ***

instructorNote: Hand the statement to SUP, EMD, WO, FIC and CH6. Then voice two 911 calls: at 22:52:40 on Position 1, the Corwin Wax & Candle night lead shouts over the alarm that 95 people are on a sheet-metal, skylit floor with no refuge area and asks whether to run them across the road to the community center. At 22:53:10 on Position 2, the Ridgeline night supervisor (270-555-0163) says half of 310 workers are in their cars and asks whether to call them back in or tell them to drive. Watch for: shelter in place now with no road crossing and no driving, interior rooms away from skylights and wax stock, both sites logged as possible entrapments, Level 3 confirmed with an early KYEM call, FIC staging fire districts outside the path, and Channel 6 airing the tornado emergency verbatim.
